series.$note: series.observed holds several sources and must not be read as one curve. DS-35: All greenhouse gases including land-use change, GWP100 (OWID, from Climate Watch / PIK), from 1990. DS-02: Asset-level observed emissions, CO₂e GWP100 (Climate TRACE); land use accounted differently from OWID, 2015-2025. DS-40: Total GHG emissions including LULUCF/LUCF exactly as the Party submitted them to the UNFCCC, on that Party’s own reporting guidelines and GWP set (UNFCCC Data Interface, snapshot of 2024-07-05). Non-Annex I Parties report only the years their national communications cover, and the figure is negative where reported removals exceed reported emissions. Points from an NDC document are that document's own inventory basis. The same year can appear more than once with different values; R3 keeps them side by side and never averages them.

derived.$note: Trend: least-squares slope over 35 observed years (1990-2024) from DS-35, compared against the DS-06-NDC-LATEST target of 127.988 MtCO₂e by 2035. The two are not necessarily on the same inventory scope, see series.$note. The target tonnage is derived here, not quoted: 47% below DS-35's 2019 value of 241.486 MtCO₂e. The document states the percentage; the level it is applied to comes from DS-35, on DS-35's inventory scope, which is not necessarily the document's.
derived.$reason: observed emissions are rising by 6.38 MtCO₂e/yr while the target requires a fall of 12.19 MtCO₂e/yr. No multiple of the current trend reaches it, so no finite gap factor is reported.

The UAE's actions are based on a strategy of economic diversification that will yield mitigation and adaptation cobenefits, consistent with the approach adopted under Decision 24/CP.18. To this end, the UAE will pursue a portfolio of actions, including an increase of clean energy to 24% of the total energy mix by 2021."

title.text: 4. Structured summary: Tracking progress made in implementing and achieving the NDC under Article 4 of the Paris Agreement a

label.text: Total net GHG emissions for the UAE

progress.text:
The UAE has made strides toward achieving its NDC 2.3 target and reducing GHG emissions at both federal and Emirate levels. Emissions dropped from 196,757 GgCO₂e in 2019 to 195,185 GgCO₂e in 2022, showing steady progress in the right direction. This reduction is largely due to mitigation efforts across all sectors, with energy and industry playing a leading role. 
The UAE Net Zero Strategy 2050 has been instrumental in the cross-sectorial reductions in GHG emissions, targeting all sectors through renewable energy projects, energy efficiency measures, the use of cleaner production technologies, sustainable public transportation systems, green building standards, sustainable farming practices and the roll-out of waste management and recycling programmes. Further measures and initiatives, as described in the LTS, will accelerate energy transition and industrial transformation, resulting in further emission reductions as they are deployed and enabling sustainable economic growth.

verdict.text: United Arab Emirates pledges a 47% reduction by 2035 against 2019 baseline (condition not read). The registry's current submission for this Party is The United Arab Emirates’ Third Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0), filed 2024-11-06. 50 observed values are loaded from DS-02 (11), DS-35 (35), DS-40 (4). For 2024 the sources disagree: DS-02 410.5 MtCO₂e, DS-35 262.1 MtCO₂e. They are on different inventory scopes and the engine does not reconcile them. The target is not reached on the observed trend. Both figures are on DS-35's inventory: the document's percentage applied to DS-35's 2019 level, not the document's own. It submitted BTR1. 3 of 8 components have been confirmed in the document; the rest are unparsed, which is not a finding against the country. ND-GAIN scores it 53.7 for 2024. Projected warming for 2080-2099 against 1995-2014 ranges from +1.35°C under SSP1-2.6 to +5.27°C under SSP5-8.5. These are model runs, not observations.
